# Adjudication Task — Chapter 26

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃26화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“그러니까……”
  6|
  7|공야청이 묘한 눈빛으로 나를 바라봤다.
  8|
  9|“바로 그 진태경 공자셨구려.”
 10|
 11|결국 이 순간이 오고야 말았다. 나는 세 번째로 기절한 혁무진의 멱살을 놓고 어색하게 웃어 보였다.
 12|
 13|“예, 제가 바로 그 진태경입니다.”
 14|
 15|야영 준비를 하고 있던 순찰조원들의 귀가 쫑긋거린다. 지금 우리는 가문으로 복귀하는 길이다.
 16|
 17|전투가 벌어진 오두막으로부터 다섯 시간을 넘게 쉬지 않고 말을 달렸다. 이동하는 내내 입을 다물고 있던 공야청이 이제야 처음으로 입을 연 것이다.
 18|
 19|‘저 새끼만 아니었어도.’
 20|
 21|나는 눈치 빠른 순찰조원에 의해 질질 끌려가는 혁무진을 노려보았다. 한 대만 더 때리고 놔줄걸.
 22|
 23|아쉬워하는 내게 공야청이 말했다.
 24|
 25|“공자의 소문은 익히 들었소.”
 26|
 27|“……그러시군요.”
 28|
 29|“세 살배기 어린아이도 공자를 알 거요. 아마 본가 최고의 유명 인사겠지.”
 30|
 31|이쯤 되면 모르는 사람을 찾는 게 빠르지 않을까 싶다.
 32|
 33|“천성이 게으르고 오만방자하다. 주색에 빠져 무공도 익히지 않는다…… 하지만 역시 강호의 소문은 믿을 게 못 되는구려. 오늘 공자가 보여 준 무위는 실로 대단했소.”
 34|
 35|“…….”
 36|
 37|강호의 소문들을 모은 강호일보, 뭐 이런 게 있다면 바로 구독 신청을 하고 싶다. 제법 신빙성이 있는데 그래.
 38|
 39|‘그보다…….’
 40|
 41|공야청 이 사람, 설마 모르고 있나?
 42|
 43|항산검문 놈들이 어떤 개수작을 부렸든 간에 이 모든 사건의 중심에는 내가 있다.
 44|
 45|그 과정에서 수많은 희생이 있다는 것은 명백한 사실.
 46|
 47|공야청과 소천이 내게 원한을 품어도 이상하지 않다. 그래서 이름을 숨긴 거였고.
 48|
 49|‘모른다면 다행이지.’
 50|
 51|잔인무도한 절정 고수에게 쫓기는 상황이다. 괜한 분란은 사양이다.
 52|
 53|“본가까지 얼마나 걸리겠소?”
 54|
 55|공야청의 말에 퍼뜩 정신이 돌아왔다.
 56|
 57|“이틀에서 사흘 정도면 도착할 수 있을 겁니다.”
 58|
 59|“하필 이럴 때 눈이라니…….”
 60|
 61|공야청이 한탄했다. 아직도 눈을 펑펑 쏟아 내는 하늘을 원망스럽게 바라본다.
 62|
 63|“공자, 최악의 상황을 대비해야겠소.”
 64|
 65|“최악의 상황이요?”
 66|
 67|폭설에 발이 묶이긴 했지만 그건 적들도 마찬가지다. 더군다나 놈들이 추격을 포기했을 가능성도 존재했다.
 68|
 69|그러나 공야청은 고개를 가로저었다.
 70|
 71|“낭인을 우습게 보지 마시오. 내력의 정순함과 익힌 무공의 수준은 떨어질지 모르나 놈들이 가진 가장 큰 무기는 따로 있소.”
 72|
 73|나는 정답을 말했다.
 74|
 75|“경험.”
 76|
 77|“맞소. 백전(百戰)을 치르며 얻은 경험. 우리를 쫓는 건 무인이 아니라 낭인이오. 같지만 아주 다른 존재지.”
 78|
 79|같지만 다른 존재. 무슨 뜻인지 알 것 같다.
 80|
 81|요컨대 놈들은 잘 훈련된 사냥개라는 뜻이다. 그 목줄을 쥔 자가 일문일살 조필이다.
 82|
 83|“조필이 진정 두려운 이유는 놈이 절정 고수이기 때문만은 아니오. 그 집요함. 악랄함. 그는 단 한 번도 의뢰에 실패하거나 표적을 놓친 적이 없소.”
 84|
 85|나는 한숨처럼 대답했다.
 86|
 87|“이번에도 마찬가지겠군요.”
 88|
 89|“아마도.”
 90|
 91|공야청이 어둠 너머를 응시했다. 마치 뭔가가 튀어나와 우리를 삼키기라도 할 것처럼.
 92|
 93|“우린 그런 놈에게 쫓기고 있는 거요.”
 94|
 95|휘이잉. 눈바람이 어둠 속으로 녹아들었다.
 96|
 97|
 98|
 99|* * *
100|
101|
102|
103|야영 준비가 끝났다. 작은 토굴을 여러 개 판 다음 나뭇가지, 낙엽 따위로 입구를 막은 조잡한 형태였지만 찬물 더운물 가릴 때가 아니다.
104|
105|“편안한 밤 되시구려.”
106|
107|공야청은 어느새 곤히 잠든 남매를 안고 사라졌다. 그의 입가에 매달린 지친 미소가 자꾸 생각났다.
108|
109|‘어른이구나.’
110|
111|살고자 했으면 진작 도망칠 수 있었을 것이다. 공야청은 무공을 익힌 고수였고 경륜 있는 무림인이니까.
112|
113|하지만 그러지 않았다. 그는 피 한 방울 섞이지 않은 어린 남매를 위해 목숨까지 걸어 가며 싸웠다.
114|
115|그래서 공야청은 좋은 어른이다.
116|
117|‘나라면 그럴 수 있을까?’
118|
119|문득 드는 의문을 털어 냈다. 이곳은 게임이다. 곧 사라질 환상에 대해 깊이 생각하는 건 좋지 않다.
120|
121|맞다, 곧 사라질 환상이다.
122|
123|‘퀘스트창 오픈.’
124|
125|띠링.
126|
127|
128|
129|퀘스트
130|
131|
132|
133|[로그아웃]
134|
135|이제 당신은 이 험난한 무림을 헤쳐 나가야 합니다.
136|
137|더욱더 강해지고, 유명해지십시오.
138|
139|언젠가 다가올 그 날을 위해…….
140|
141|
142|
143|등급 : 메인 퀘스트
144|
145|제한 : 진태경
146|
147|임무 : [일류] 경지 달성 (미완료)
148|
149|         Lv.30 달성 (24/30)
150|
151|         명성 500 달성 (250/500)
152|
153|보상 : [로그아웃]
154|
155|
156|
157|
158|
159|적들을 처리하고 받은 경험치와 명성. 거기에 퀘스트 보상까지. 슬슬 이 험산의 정상이 보인다.
160|
161|상태창을 열어 남은 포인트를 모두 분배하니 지쳐 있던 몸에 활력이 돈다.
162|
163|‘거의 다 왔어.’
164|
165|이번 고비만 넘기면 된다. 일문일살 조필. 얼굴도 모르는 그놈만 피하면 이 지긋지긋한 여정에 종지부를 찍을 수 있다.
166|
167|하지만 또 다른 문제가 있었다.
168|
169|‘레벨이나 명성은 어찌어찌 채운다 치고, 이놈의 경지는 어떻게 올리는 거야?’
170|
171|처음 튜토리얼 퀘스트를 깨기 시작할 무렵 능력치 분배로 삼류에서 이류로 경지를 올린 적이 있다. 그런데 그 후로는 영 깜깜무소식이다.
172|
173|‘도대체 뭐가 부족한 거지?’
174|
175|무림에서 나는 비상식적인 존재다. 누구보다 빠르게 무공을 익히고 능력치를 올릴 수 있다. 여러 부분에서 시스템의 힘을 빌려 강해졌다.
176|
177|그게 널리고 널린 이류 주제에 어지간한 일류 무림인을 말 그대로 발라 버릴 수 있었던 이유다.
178|
179|그런데 정작 내가 일류가 아니라니!
180|
181|‘진위경한테라도 물어볼걸.’
182|
183|처음엔 계속 스탯이나 공력을 올리면 되겠지, 싶었는데 근래 들어서 뭔가 헛짚고 있다는 생각이 든다.
184|
185|‘레벨? 스탯? 공력?’
186|
187|그게 뭘까. 이 퍼즐을 완성할 마지막 한 조각이.
188|
189|답은 금방 나왔다.
190|
191|‘모르면 찾아야지.’
192|
193|지금까지 해 왔던 것처럼. 걷다 보면 출구는 나온다.
194|
195|나는 가부좌를 틀고 호흡했다. 단전에 똬리 튼 공력이 내 부름에 응답했다.
196|
197|
198|
199|* * *
200|
201|
202|
203|“놓쳤군.”
204|
205|조필이 중얼거렸다. 독사처럼 까만 눈동자가 주위를 훑었다.
206|
207|놈들을 놓쳤다. 그러나 흔적은 남았다. 미세하게 남은 그 흔적들이 새로운 이정표가 될 것이다.
208|
209|“스무 명 전후. 약 두 시진 전에 자리를 떴습니다.”
210|
211|수하의 보고에 조필이 고개를 끄덕였다. 무공은 삼류지만 추종술은 절정이다. 그의 밑에는 이런 사냥개들이 수두룩했다.
212|
213|‘두 시진이라.’
214|
215|어느새 거리가 두 시진으로 좁혀졌다. 도망자들을 따라잡기까지 어느 정도의 시간이 걸릴까?
216|
217|길어야 반나절이다.
218|
219|‘있는 힘을 다해 도망쳤어야지. 뒤도 안 돌아보고. 거추장스러운 혹은 떼고 낙오자는 버리고 악착같이 뛰었어야지.’
220|
221|그랬다면 거리는 좁혀지지 않았을 것이다. 그러나 놈들은 방심했다. 폭설에 발이 묶였다고 생각했을 것이고, 그 차이가 지금의 상황을 만들었다.
222|
223|‘나는 좀 다르거든.’
224|
225|지난밤은 길었다. 추적에는 이골이 난 수하 중에서도 낙오자가 생길 정도였다. 폭설이 내리는 산중에서의 낙오란 죽음과 동의어다.
226|
227|전장에서의 죽음과 다른 점이 있다면 조금 천천히 죽는다는 것뿐이다. 그래서 조필은 지시했다.
228|
229|
230|
231|‘죽여.’
232|
233|
234|
235|호랑이는 죽어서 가죽을, 사람은 이름을 남긴다고 했다.
236|
237|하지만 조필의 생각은 달랐다. 일평생 뒷골목을 전전하던 삼류 인생에게 남길 이름이 있겠나. 가죽이라도 남겨야지.
238|
239|발가벗겨진 스무 구의 시신을 뒤로하고 그들은 계속 나아갔다. 그렇게 긴 밤이 끝나고 동틀 무렵, 놈들의 흔적을 발견할 수 있었다.
240|
241|‘곧 만날 수 있겠군, 친구.’
242|
243|조필의 입꼬리가 올라갔다. 오랜만에 그의 흥미를 끈 수수께끼의 고수다. 굳어 있던 심장이 펄떡거리며 뛰었다.
244|
245|
246|
247|* * *
248|
249|
250|
251|부르르.
252|
253|“어흐. 뭐야.”
254|
255|순간 오한이 들었다. 팔뚝을 들어 보니 닭살이 오소소 돋아 있다. 지금이 소설의 한 장면이었다면, 주인공은 왠지 꺼림칙하다는 말과 함께 가던 길을 갔을 것이다.
256|
257|하지만 나는 다르다. 확실한 심증을 갖고 움직인다.
258|
259|“야. 잽싸게 튀어와.”
260|
261|보이지 않지만 느껴진다. 뒤에서 터벅터벅 걷고 있던 누군가의 발걸음이 움찔한다.
262|
263|“왜, 왜요.”
264|
265|“셋 센다. 하나, 둘. 셋.”
266|
267|셋을 셈과 동시에 혁무진이 잽싸게 옆에 붙었다.
268|
269|“너지?”
270|
271|“예?”
272|
273|“너잖아. 솔직히 말하면 봐준다.”
274|
275|“뭘요? 저 아닙니다!”
276|
277|나는 찐빵처럼 부푼 녀석의 얼굴을 가만히 응시했다.
278|
279|“방금 뒤에서 나 욕했지?”
280|
281|“헛.”
282|
283|“욕한 거 맞지?”
284|
285|“마, 맞습니다…….”
286|
287|역시 이 자식이었군. 내가 손을 들어 올리자 혁무진이 눈을 질끈 감는다.
288|
289|세 번 정도 얻어터지자 녀석은 전의를 잃어버렸다. 거기에 더해 생활의 지혜도 터득했다.
290|
291|피하면 더 맞는다는 사실을.
292|
293|“좋아. 솔직히 말했으니 이번만은 봐준다.”
294|
295|혁무진이 고개를 번쩍 치켜든다.
296|
297|“정말이십니까?”
298|
299|내가 따뜻한 미소를 지어 보였다.
300|
301|“물론. 하지만 앞으로도 나를 속일 생각은 하지 마라. 관심법으로 널 지켜보고 있을 테니.”
302|
303|혁무진은 마구니가 가득 낀 눈빛으로 나를 바라보다가 제 자리로 튀어 갔다. 시간만 넉넉했다면 철퇴로 머리를 으깨 주었을 텐데. 나는 아쉬움을 삼키고 계속 걸었다.
304|
305|“관심법이 모야?”
306|
307|재잘거리는 목소리에 귀가 간지럽다. 소천의 여동생인 소율이다. 다섯 살이라고 했나? 녀석은 내 배낭에 쏙 들어갈 정도로 작았다.
308|
309|“무공이야?”
310|
311|“비슷하지.”
312|
313|“관심법, 세?”
314|
315|“엄청 세지.”
316|
317|“와! 소율이도 관심법 배우고 싶어요!”
318|
319|“근데 눈이 애꾸여야 돼.”
320|
321|“헉!”
322|
323|고개를 슬쩍 돌려보니 화들짝 놀란 소율의 얼굴이 보인다. 휘둥그레진 눈동자가 장난 아니게 귀엽다.
324|
325|‘하연이도 저랬었는데.’
326|
327|지금이야 징그러운 여동생이지만 어릴 때는 아기 천사가 따로 없었다. 아역 모델 제의도 받고 그랬었는데…….
328|
329|딱 그 시절의 하연이를 업고 다니는 기분이다.
330|
331|“나한테 배울래?”
332|
333|“……소율이는 무공 같은 거 안 좋아해요. 참한 규수가 될래요.”
334|
335|“그것도 좋지.”
336|
337|“으응. 아저씨는 무공 좋아해요?”
338|

I could finally see the summit of this treacherous mountain.

[P66]
I opened my Status Window and distributed all my remaining points. Energy flowed back into my exhausted body.

[P67]
*I’m almost there.*

[P68]
I just had to get past this final hurdle. If I could avoid Jopil, One Question, One Kill—the bastard whose face I didn’t even know—I could finally bring this miserable journey to an end.

[P69]
But there was another problem.

[P70]
*Let’s say I somehow fill up my Level and Fame. How the hell am I supposed to raise my realm?*

[P71]
Back when I first started clearing the tutorial Quests, distributing my stats had raised my realm from Third Rate to Second Rate. Since then, nothing.

[P72]
*What the hell am I missing?*

[P73]
I was an absurd existence in Murim. I could learn martial arts and raise my stats faster than anyone else. The System had helped me grow stronger in all kinds of ways.

[P74]
That was how a dime-a-dozen Second Rate martial artist like me could literally wipe the floor with most First Rate martial artists.

[P75]
And yet I wasn’t First Rate!

[P76]
*I should’ve asked Jin Wikyung.*

[P77]
At first, I had assumed I just needed to keep raising my stats or internal energy. Lately, though, I had begun to suspect I was barking up the wrong tree.

[P78]
*Level? Stats? Internal energy?*

[P79]
What was it? What final piece did I need to complete the puzzle?

[P80]
The answer came quickly.

[P81]
*If I don’t know, I’ll find out.*

[P82]
Just as I always had. If I kept walking, I would eventually find the exit.

[P83]
I sat cross-legged and steadied my breathing. The internal energy coiled within my dantian answered my call.

[P84]
* * *

[P85]
“We lost them.”

[P86]
Jopil muttered as his black, viper-like eyes swept across the surroundings.

[P87]
They had lost the fugitives. But traces remained, faint signs that would serve as new guideposts.

[P88]
“About twenty people. They left roughly two shichen ago.”[^1]

[P89]
Jopil nodded at his subordinate’s report. The man’s martial arts were only Third Rate, but his tracking skills had reached the Peak. Jopil had countless hunting dogs like him under his command.

[P90]
*Two shichen.*

[P91]
The gap had already narrowed to two shichen. How much longer would it take them to catch the fugitives?

[P92]
Half a day at most.

[P93]
*They should have run with everything they had. Without looking back. They should have cast off every burden, abandoned anyone who fell behind, and run for their lives.*

[P94]
If they had, the gap would never have narrowed. But they had let their guard down. They must have assumed the blizzard would stop their pursuers as well.

[P95]
That misjudgment had brought them to this point.

[P96]
*But I’m a little different.*

[P97]
The previous night had been long. Even among his subordinates, men well accustomed to pursuit, some had fallen behind.

[P98]
In the mountains during a blizzard, falling behind was no different from death.

[P99]
The only difference from dying on the battlefield was that it took a little longer.

[P100]
That was why Jopil had given the order.

[P101]
*Kill them.*

[P102]
They said a tiger left its hide when it died, while a person left their name.

[P103]
Jopil disagreed. What name could be left behind by Third Rate nobodies who had spent their whole lives drifting through back alleys?

[P104]
They might as well leave their hides.

[P105]
Leaving twenty stripped corpses behind, the group had pressed onward. When the long night finally ended, they discovered the fugitives’ trail shortly before dawn.

[P106]
*We’ll meet soon, friend.*

[P107]
The corners of Jopil’s mouth curled upward. This mysterious master was the first person in a long time to pique his interest.

[P108]
His heart, stiff for so long, began to pound.

[P109]
* * *

[P110]
I shuddered.

[P111]
“Ugh. What the hell?”

[P112]
A sudden chill ran through me. I raised my arm and found it covered in goose bumps.

[P113]
If this had been a scene in a novel, the protagonist would have muttered that something felt wrong, then continued on his way.

[P114]
But I was different. I acted on firm suspicions.

[P115]
“Hey. Get over here, now.”

[P116]
I couldn’t see him, but I could sense him. The footsteps of someone trudging along behind me faltered.

[P117]
“W-why?”

[P118]
“I’m counting to three. One, two… three.”

[P119]
The moment I reached three, Hyuk Mujin hurried over and stuck to my side.

[P120]
“It was you, wasn’t it?”

[P121]
“What?”

[P122]
“You know what I mean. Tell me the truth and I’ll let it slide.”

[P123]
“What are you talking about? It wasn’t me!”

[P124]
I silently studied his face, swollen like a steamed bun.

[P125]
“You were cursing me behind my back just now, weren’t you?”

[P126]
“Gasp.”

[P127]
“You were, weren’t you?”

[P128]
“I-I was…”

[P129]
So it really had been this bastard. When I raised my hand, Hyuk Mujin squeezed his eyes shut.

[P130]
After being beaten unconscious three times, he had lost all will to resist. He had also learned a valuable lesson in life:

[P131]
Dodging only meant getting hit more.

[P132]
“Fine. Since you told the truth, I’ll let it slide this once.”

[P133]
Hyuk Mujin’s head shot up.

[P134]
“Really?”

[P135]
I gave him a warm smile.

[P136]
“Of course. But don’t even think about deceiving me again. I’ll be watching you with my mind-reading technique.”

[P137]
Hyuk Mujin stared at me with eyes full of demonic rage, then darted back to his place. If only we’d had more time, I could have smashed his head in with a mace.

[P138]
Swallowing my disappointment, I kept walking.

[P139]
“What’s a mind-reading technique?”

[P140]
The chirping voice tickled my ear. It belonged to Soyul, Socheon’s little sister. Had they said she was five?

[P141]
She was small enough to fit inside my backpack.

[P142]
“Is it martial arts?”

[P143]
“Something like that.”

[P144]
“Is mind-reading strong?”

[P145]
“Very strong.”

[P146]
“Wow! Soyul wants to learn mind-reading too!”

[P147]
“But you have to be one-eyed.”

[P148]
“Gasp!”

[P149]
I glanced back and saw Soyul staring at me in shock, her eyes enormous. She was ridiculously cute.

[P150]
*Hayeon used to be like that too.*

[P151]
These days she was a creepy little sister, but when she was young, she had been a perfect little angel. She had even received offers to become a child model…

[P152]
Carrying Soyul on my back felt just like carrying Hayeon at that age.

[P153]
“Want me to teach you?”

[P154]
“…Soyul doesn’t like martial arts. I’m going to become a proper young lady.”

[P155]
“That’s good too.”

[P156]
“Mm. Uncle, do you like martial arts?”

[P157]
“Me?”

[P158]
“My brother says you’re really strong. Dad said only people who work hard can become strong.”

[P159]
“Your dad said that?”

[P160]
“Yes. My dad is really strong too. That’s because…”

[P161]
Soyul chattered excitedly for a long while before sticking out her lower lip.

[P162]
“Soyul misses Dad. But I guess Dad doesn’t miss me. My brother says he went on a trip with Mom and left me and my brother behind.”

[P163]
My heart dropped.

[P164]
An old memory filled my vision. In a funeral hall draped in black and white, little Hayeon had searched for our father, and I had been forced to tell her an obvious lie.

[P165]
Just as Socheon had done for Soyul.

[P166]
There had been nothing else he could say.

[P167]
“…I see.”

[P168]
What else could I say?

[P169]
I looked at Socheon, who was following in the middle of the formation. He was breathing hard, his clothes drenched in sweat.

[P170]
*He must be exhausted.*

[P171]
He had far more willpower than anyone his age should have needed. The saying that suffering made people mature was fucking bullshit, but it was also true.

[P172]
Socheon hadn’t fallen behind even once, and even the other reconnaissance squad members marveled at his determination.

[P173]
*But the real problem is someone else.*

[P174]
Gong Yacheong.

[P175]
He still hadn’t recovered from his injuries, and his face was deathly pale. If not for the remarkable effects of the fasting pills I had given him and the qi circulation he had performed the previous night, he might have collapsed long ago.

[P176]
*At this rate, they’ll catch us.*

[P177]
Even after sunrise, the deep snow showed no sign of melting. I was leading the way and breaking a path through it, but everyone was exhausted, and our pace kept slowing.

[P178]
Worse, we had an injured man and two children with us.

[P179]
*Should I run away on my own?*

[P180]
The thought came to me in an instant.

[P181]
It was a game. So what?

[P182]
Gong Yacheong, the young siblings, every member of the reconnaissance squad—they were all artificially created intelligences. Nothing more than NPCs.

[P183]
But me?

[P184]
I was alive. I was the only real person among them. The only one who truly existed.

[P185]
But…

[P186]
*Fuck. It’s such a simple problem… So why am I like this?*

[P187]
An inexplicable revulsion surged through me. It was so intense that it startled me, leaving me shaken.

[P188]
*Why?*

[P189]
I didn’t know.

[P190]
For hours afterward, I failed to find the answer.

[P191]
And then night fell.

[P192]
[^1]: A shichen is a traditional Chinese unit of time equal to roughly two hours.
```

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

“How long will it take us to reach your family?”

[P27]
Gong Yacheong’s question snapped me back to reality.

[P28]
“We should arrive in two or three days.”

[P29]
“Of all times, it had to snow now…”

[P30]
Gong Yacheong sighed and glared resentfully at the sky, which was still dumping snow on us.

[P31]
“Young Master, we should prepare for the worst.”

[P32]
“The worst?”

[P33]
The blizzard had slowed us down, but it had to be slowing our enemies as well. There was even a chance they had abandoned the chase.

[P34]
But Gong Yacheong shook his head.

[P35]
“Don’t underestimate wandering martial artists. Their internal energy may be less refined, and the martial arts they’ve learned may be inferior, but their greatest weapon lies elsewhere.”

[P36]
I gave him the answer.

[P37]
“Experience.”

[P38]
“Exactly. Experience gained through a hundred battles. The ones chasing us aren’t merely martial artists. They’re wandering martial artists. The two may seem alike, but they’re entirely different creatures.”

[P39]
Alike, yet different. I thought I understood what he meant.

[P40]
In short, they were well-trained hunting dogs. And the man holding their leash was Jopil, One Question, One Kill.

[P41]
“What makes Jopil truly frightening isn’t simply that he’s a Peak master. It’s his persistence. His viciousness. He has never once failed a commission or allowed a target to escape.”

[P42]
I answered with a sigh.

[P43]
“This time won’t be any different, then.”

[P44]
“Probably not.”

[P45]
Gong Yacheong stared into the darkness ahead as though something might leap out and swallow us whole.

[P46]
“That is the sort of man pursuing us.”

[P47]
Whoosh.

[P48]
The snow-laden wind vanished into the darkness.

[P49]
* * *

[P50]
We finished making camp. We had dug several small hollows and covered their entrances with branches, fallen leaves, and whatever else we could find. The shelters were crude, but this was no time to be choosy.

[P51]
“Have a restful night.”

[P52]
Gong Yacheong disappeared into one of them, carrying the siblings, who had already fallen fast asleep. I couldn’t stop thinking about the weary smile hanging from the corner of his mouth.

[P53]
*He really is an adult.*

[P54]
If all he had wanted was to survive, he could have fled long ago. Gong Yacheong was a skilled martial artist and a seasoned man of Murim.

[P55]
But he hadn’t.

[P56]
He had risked his life fighting for two children who didn’t share a drop of his blood.

[P57]
That was why Gong Yacheong was a good adult.

[P58]
*Could I do the same?*

[P59]
I shook off the question as soon as it arose. This was a game. It wasn’t wise to think too deeply about an illusion that would soon disappear.

[P60]
That was right. An illusion that would soon disappear.

[P61]
*Open Quest Window.*

[P62]
Ding.

[P63]
> **System**
>
> **Quest**
>
> **Logout**
>
> You must now make your way through this harsh Murim.
>
> Become stronger. Become famous.
>
> For the day that will come someday…
>
> **Grade:** Main Quest
>
> **Limit:** Jin Taekyung
>
> **Task:** Reach the First Rate realm — Incomplete  
>          Reach Lv. 30 — 24/30  
>          Reach Fame 500 — 250/500
>
> **Reward:** **Logout**

[P64]
The EXP and Fame I had gained from dealing with the enemies, plus the Quest reward.

[P65]
I could finally see the summit of this treacherous mountain.

[P66]
I opened my Status Window and distributed all my remaining points. Energy flowed back into my exhausted body.

[P67]
*I’m almost there.*

[P68]
I just had to get past this final hurdle. If I could avoid Jopil, One Question, One Kill—the bastard whose face I didn’t even know—I could finally bring this miserable journey to an end.

[P69]
But there was another problem.

[P70]
*Let’s say I somehow fill up my Level and Fame. How the hell am I supposed to raise my realm?*

[P71]
Back when I first started clearing the tutorial Quests, distributing my stats had raised my realm from Third Rate to Second Rate. Since then, nothing.

[P72]
*What the hell am I missing?*

[P73]
I was an absurd existence in Murim. I could learn martial arts and raise my stats faster than anyone else. The System had helped me grow stronger in all kinds of ways.

[P74]
That was how a dime-a-dozen Second Rate martial artist like me could literally wipe the floor with most First Rate martial artists.

[P75]
And yet I wasn’t First Rate!

[P76]
*I should’ve asked Jin Wikyung.*

[P77]
At first, I had assumed I just needed to keep raising my stats or internal energy. Lately, though, I had begun to suspect I was barking up the wrong tree.

[P78]
*Level? Stats? Internal energy?*

[P79]
What was it? What final piece did I need to complete the puzzle?

[P80]
The answer came quickly.

[P81]
*If I don’t know, I’ll find out.*

[P82]
Just as I always had. If I kept walking, I would eventually find the exit.

[P83]
I sat cross-legged and steadied my breathing. The internal energy coiled within my dantian answered my call.

[P84]
* * *

[P85]
“We lost them.”

[P86]
Jopil muttered as his black, viper-like eyes swept across the surroundings.

[P87]
They had lost the fugitives. But traces remained, faint signs that would serve as new guideposts.

[P88]
“About twenty people. They left roughly two shichen ago.”[^1]

[P89]
Jopil nodded at his subordinate’s report. The man’s martial arts were only Third Rate, but his tracking skills had reached the Peak. Jopil had countless hunting dogs like him under his command.

[P90]
*Two shichen.*

[P91]
The gap had already narrowed to two shichen. How much longer would it take them to catch the fugitives?

[P92]
Half a day at most.

[P93]
*They should have run with everything they had. Without looking back. They should have cast off every burden, abandoned anyone who fell behind, and run for their lives.*

[P94]
If they had, the gap would never have narrowed. But they had let their guard down. They must have assumed the blizzard would stop their pursuers as well.

[P95]
That misjudgment had brought them to this point.

[P96]
*But I’m a little different.*

[P97]
The previous night had been long. Even among his subordinates, men well accustomed to pursuit, some had fallen behind.

[P98]
In the mountains during a blizzard, falling behind was no different from death.

[P99]
The only difference from dying on the battlefield was that it took a little longer.

[P100]
That was why Jopil had given the order.

[P101]
*Kill them.*

[P102]
They said a tiger left its hide when it died, while a person left their name.

[P103]
Jopil disagreed. What name could be left behind by Third Rate nobodies who had spent their whole lives drifting through back alleys?

[P104]
They might as well leave their hides.

[P105]
Leaving twenty stripped corpses behind, the group had pressed onward. When the long night finally ended, they discovered the fugitives’ trail shortly before dawn.

[P106]
*We’ll meet soon, friend.*

[P107]
The corners of Jopil’s mouth curled upward. This mysterious master was the first person in a long time to pique his interest.

[P108]
His heart, stiff for so long, began to pound.

[P109]
* * *

[P110]
I shuddered.

[P111]
“Ugh. What the hell?”

[P112]
A sudden chill ran through me. I raised my arm and found it covered in goose bumps.

[P113]
If this had been a scene in a novel, the protagonist would have muttered that something felt wrong, then continued on his way.

[P114]
But I was different. I acted on firm suspicions.

[P115]
“Hey. Get over here, now.”

[P116]
I couldn’t see him, but I could sense him. The footsteps of someone trudging along behind me faltered.

[P117]
“W-why?”

[P118]
“I’m counting to three. One, two… three.”

[P119]
The moment I reached three, Hyuk Mujin hurried over and stuck to my side.

[P120]
“It was you, wasn’t it?”

[P121]
“What?”

[P122]
“You know what I mean. Tell me the truth and I’ll let it slide.”

[P123]
“What are you talking about? It wasn’t me!”

[P124]
I silently studied his face, swollen like a steamed bun.

[P125]
“You were cursing me behind my back just now, weren’t you?”

[P126]
“Gasp.”

[P127]
“You were, weren’t you?”

[P128]
“I-I was…”

[P129]
So it really had been this bastard. When I raised my hand, Hyuk Mujin squeezed his eyes shut.

[P130]
After being beaten unconscious three times, he had lost all will to resist. He had also learned a valuable lesson in life:

[P131]
Dodging only meant getting hit more.

[P132]
“Fine. Since you told the truth, I’ll let it slide this once.”

[P133]
Hyuk Mujin’s head shot up.

[P134]
“Really?”

[P135]
I gave him a warm smile.

[P136]
“Of course. But don’t even think about deceiving me again. I’ll be watching you with my mind-reading technique.”

[P137]
Hyuk Mujin stared at me with eyes full of demonic rage, then darted back to his place. If only we’d had more time, I could have smashed his head in with a mace.

[P138]
Swallowing my disappointment, I kept walking.

[P139]
“What’s a mind-reading technique?”

[P140]
The chirping voice tickled my ear. It belonged to Soyul, Socheon’s little sister. Had they said she was five?

[P141]
She was small enough to fit inside my backpack.

[P142]
“Is it martial arts?”

[P143]
“Something like that.”

[P144]
“Is mind-reading strong?”

[P145]
“Very strong.”

[P146]
“Wow! Soyul wants to learn mind-reading too!”

[P147]
“But you have to be one-eyed.”

[P148]
“Gasp!”

[P149]
I glanced back and saw Soyul staring at me in shock, her eyes enormous. She was ridiculously cute.

[P150]
*Hayeon used to be like that too.*

[P151]
These days she was a creepy little sister, but when she was young, she had been a perfect little angel. She had even received offers to become a child model…

[P152]
Carrying Soyul on my back felt just like carrying Hayeon at that age.

[P153]
“Want me to teach you?”

[P154]
“…Soyul doesn’t like martial arts. I’m going to become a proper young lady.”

[P155]
“That’s good too.”

[P156]
“Mm. Uncle, do you like martial arts?”

[P157]
“Me?”

[P158]
“My brother says you’re really strong. Dad said only people who work hard can become strong.”

[P159]
“Your dad said that?”

[P160]
“Yes. My dad is really strong too. That’s because…”

[P161]
Soyul chattered excitedly for a long while before sticking out her lower lip.

[P162]
“Soyul misses Dad. But I guess Dad doesn’t miss me. My brother says he went on a trip with Mom and left me and my brother behind.”

[P163]
My heart dropped.

[P164]
An old memory filled my vision. In a funeral hall draped in black and white, little Hayeon had searched for our father, and I had been forced to tell her an obvious lie.

[P165]
Just as Socheon had done for Soyul.

[P166]
There had been nothing else he could say.

[P167]
“…I see.”

[P168]
What else could I say?

[P169]
I looked at Socheon, who was following in the middle of the formation. He was breathing hard, his clothes drenched in sweat.

[P170]
*He must be exhausted.*

[P171]
He had far more willpower than anyone his age should have needed. The saying that suffering made people mature was fucking bullshit, but it was also true.

[P172]
Socheon hadn’t fallen behind even once, and even the other reconnaissance squad members marveled at his determination.

[P173]
*But the real problem is someone else.*

[P174]
Gong Yacheong.

[P175]
He still hadn’t recovered from his injuries, and his face was deathly pale. If not for the remarkable effects of the fasting pills I had given him and the qi circulation he had performed the previous night, he might have collapsed long ago.

[P176]
*At this rate, they’ll catch us.*

[P177]
Even after sunrise, the deep snow showed no sign of melting. I was leading the way and breaking a path through it, but everyone was exhausted, and our pace kept slowing.

[P178]
Worse, we had an injured man and two children with us.

[P179]
*Should I run away on my own?*

[P180]
The thought came to me in an instant.

[P181]
It was a game. So what?

[P182]
Gong Yacheong, the young siblings, every member of the reconnaissance squad—they were all artificially created intelligences. Nothing more than NPCs.

[P183]
But me?

[P184]
I was alive. I was the only real person among them. The only one who truly existed.

[P185]
But…

[P186]
*Fuck. It’s such a simple problem… So why am I like this?*

[P187]
An inexplicable revulsion surged through me. It was so intense that it startled me, leaving me shaken.

[P188]
*Why?*

[P189]
I didn’t know.

[P190]
For hours afterward, I failed to find the answer.

[P191]
And then night fell.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 26

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃26화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“그러니까……”
  6|
  7|공야청이 묘한 눈빛으로 나를 바라봤다.
  8|
  9|“바로 그 진태경 공자셨구려.”
 10|
 11|결국 이 순간이 오고야 말았다. 나는 세 번째로 기절한 혁무진의 멱살을 놓고 어색하게 웃어 보였다.
 12|
 13|“예, 제가 바로 그 진태경입니다.”
 14|
 15|야영 준비를 하고 있던 순찰조원들의 귀가 쫑긋거린다. 지금 우리는 가문으로 복귀하는 길이다.
 16|
 17|전투가 벌어진 오두막으로부터 다섯 시간을 넘게 쉬지 않고 말을 달렸다. 이동하는 내내 입을 다물고 있던 공야청이 이제야 처음으로 입을 연 것이다.
 18|
 19|‘저 새끼만 아니었어도.’
 20|
 21|나는 눈치 빠른 순찰조원에 의해 질질 끌려가는 혁무진을 노려보았다. 한 대만 더 때리고 놔줄걸.
 22|
 23|아쉬워하는 내게 공야청이 말했다.
 24|
 25|“공자의 소문은 익히 들었소.”
 26|
 27|“……그러시군요.”
 28|
 29|“세 살배기 어린아이도 공자를 알 거요. 아마 본가 최고의 유명 인사겠지.”
 30|
 31|이쯤 되면 모르는 사람을 찾는 게 빠르지 않을까 싶다.
 32|
 33|“천성이 게으르고 오만방자하다. 주색에 빠져 무공도 익히지 않는다…… 하지만 역시 강호의 소문은 믿을 게 못 되는구려. 오늘 공자가 보여 준 무위는 실로 대단했소.”
 34|
 35|“…….”
 36|
 37|강호의 소문들을 모은 강호일보, 뭐 이런 게 있다면 바로 구독 신청을 하고 싶다. 제법 신빙성이 있는데 그래.
 38|
 39|‘그보다…….’
 40|
 41|공야청 이 사람, 설마 모르고 있나?
 42|
 43|항산검문 놈들이 어떤 개수작을 부렸든 간에 이 모든 사건의 중심에는 내가 있다.
 44|
 45|그 과정에서 수많은 희생이 있다는 것은 명백한 사실.
 46|
 47|공야청과 소천이 내게 원한을 품어도 이상하지 않다. 그래서 이름을 숨긴 거였고.
 48|
 49|‘모른다면 다행이지.’
 50|
 51|잔인무도한 절정 고수에게 쫓기는 상황이다. 괜한 분란은 사양이다.
 52|
 53|“본가까지 얼마나 걸리겠소?”
 54|
 55|공야청의 말에 퍼뜩 정신이 돌아왔다.
 56|
 57|“이틀에서 사흘 정도면 도착할 수 있을 겁니다.”
 58|
 59|“하필 이럴 때 눈이라니…….”
 60|
 61|공야청이 한탄했다. 아직도 눈을 펑펑 쏟아 내는 하늘을 원망스럽게 바라본다.
 62|
 63|“공자, 최악의 상황을 대비해야겠소.”
 64|
 65|“최악의 상황이요?”
 66|
 67|폭설에 발이 묶이긴 했지만 그건 적들도 마찬가지다. 더군다나 놈들이 추격을 포기했을 가능성도 존재했다.
 68|
 69|그러나 공야청은 고개를 가로저었다.
 70|
 71|“낭인을 우습게 보지 마시오. 내력의 정순함과 익힌 무공의 수준은 떨어질지 모르나 놈들이 가진 가장 큰 무기는 따로 있소.”
 72|
 73|나는 정답을 말했다.
 74|
 75|“경험.”
 76|
 77|“맞소. 백전(百戰)을 치르며 얻은 경험. 우리를 쫓는 건 무인이 아니라 낭인이오. 같지만 아주 다른 존재지.”
 78|
 79|같지만 다른 존재. 무슨 뜻인지 알 것 같다.
 80|
 81|요컨대 놈들은 잘 훈련된 사냥개라는 뜻이다. 그 목줄을 쥔 자가 일문일살 조필이다.
 82|
 83|“조필이 진정 두려운 이유는 놈이 절정 고수이기 때문만은 아니오. 그 집요함. 악랄함. 그는 단 한 번도 의뢰에 실패하거나 표적을 놓친 적이 없소.”
 84|
 85|나는 한숨처럼 대답했다.
 86|
 87|“이번에도 마찬가지겠군요.”
 88|
 89|“아마도.”
 90|
 91|공야청이 어둠 너머를 응시했다. 마치 뭔가가 튀어나와 우리를 삼키기라도 할 것처럼.
 92|
 93|“우린 그런 놈에게 쫓기고 있는 거요.”
 94|
 95|휘이잉. 눈바람이 어둠 속으로 녹아들었다.
 96|
 97|
 98|
 99|* * *
100|
101|
102|
103|야영 준비가 끝났다. 작은 토굴을 여러 개 판 다음 나뭇가지, 낙엽 따위로 입구를 막은 조잡한 형태였지만 찬물 더운물 가릴 때가 아니다.
104|
105|“편안한 밤 되시구려.”
106|
107|공야청은 어느새 곤히 잠든 남매를 안고 사라졌다. 그의 입가에 매달린 지친 미소가 자꾸 생각났다.
108|
109|‘어른이구나.’
110|
111|살고자 했으면 진작 도망칠 수 있었을 것이다. 공야청은 무공을 익힌 고수였고 경륜 있는 무림인이니까.
112|
113|하지만 그러지 않았다. 그는 피 한 방울 섞이지 않은 어린 남매를 위해 목숨까지 걸어 가며 싸웠다.
114|
115|그래서 공야청은 좋은 어른이다.
116|
117|‘나라면 그럴 수 있을까?’
118|
119|문득 드는 의문을 털어 냈다. 이곳은 게임이다. 곧 사라질 환상에 대해 깊이 생각하는 건 좋지 않다.
120|
121|맞다, 곧 사라질 환상이다.
122|
123|‘퀘스트창 오픈.’
124|
125|띠링.
126|
127|
128|
129|퀘스트
130|
131|
132|
133|[로그아웃]
134|
135|이제 당신은 이 험난한 무림을 헤쳐 나가야 합니다.
136|
137|더욱더 강해지고, 유명해지십시오.
138|
139|언젠가 다가올 그 날을 위해…….
140|
141|
142|
143|등급 : 메인 퀘스트
144|
145|제한 : 진태경
146|
147|임무 : [일류] 경지 달성 (미완료)
148|
149|         Lv.30 달성 (24/30)
150|
151|         명성 500 달성 (250/500)
152|
153|보상 : [로그아웃]
154|
155|
156|
157|
158|
159|적들을 처리하고 받은 경험치와 명성. 거기에 퀘스트 보상까지. 슬슬 이 험산의 정상이 보인다.
160|
161|상태창을 열어 남은 포인트를 모두 분배하니 지쳐 있던 몸에 활력이 돈다.
162|
163|‘거의 다 왔어.’
164|
165|이번 고비만 넘기면 된다. 일문일살 조필. 얼굴도 모르는 그놈만 피하면 이 지긋지긋한 여정에 종지부를 찍을 수 있다.
166|
167|하지만 또 다른 문제가 있었다.
168|
169|‘레벨이나 명성은 어찌어찌 채운다 치고, 이놈의 경지는 어떻게 올리는 거야?’
170|
171|처음 튜토리얼 퀘스트를 깨기 시작할 무렵 능력치 분배로 삼류에서 이류로 경지를 올린 적이 있다. 그런데 그 후로는 영 깜깜무소식이다.
172|
173|‘도대체 뭐가 부족한 거지?’
174|
175|무림에서 나는 비상식적인 존재다. 누구보다 빠르게 무공을 익히고 능력치를 올릴 수 있다. 여러 부분에서 시스템의 힘을 빌려 강해졌다.
176|
177|그게 널리고 널린 이류 주제에 어지간한 일류 무림인을 말 그대로 발라 버릴 수 있었던 이유다.
178|
179|그런데 정작 내가 일류가 아니라니!
180|
181|‘진위경한테라도 물어볼걸.’
182|
183|처음엔 계속 스탯이나 공력을 올리면 되겠지, 싶었는데 근래 들어서 뭔가 헛짚고 있다는 생각이 든다.
184|
185|‘레벨? 스탯? 공력?’
186|
187|그게 뭘까. 이 퍼즐을 완성할 마지막 한 조각이.
188|
189|답은 금방 나왔다.
190|
191|‘모르면 찾아야지.’
192|
193|지금까지 해 왔던 것처럼. 걷다 보면 출구는 나온다.
194|
195|나는 가부좌를 틀고 호흡했다. 단전에 똬리 튼 공력이 내 부름에 응답했다.
196|
197|
198|
199|* * *
200|
201|
202|
203|“놓쳤군.”
204|
205|조필이 중얼거렸다. 독사처럼 까만 눈동자가 주위를 훑었다.
206|
207|놈들을 놓쳤다. 그러나 흔적은 남았다. 미세하게 남은 그 흔적들이 새로운 이정표가 될 것이다.
208|
209|“스무 명 전후. 약 두 시진 전에 자리를 떴습니다.”
210|
211|수하의 보고에 조필이 고개를 끄덕였다. 무공은 삼류지만 추종술은 절정이다. 그의 밑에는 이런 사냥개들이 수두룩했다.
212|
213|‘두 시진이라.’
214|
215|어느새 거리가 두 시진으로 좁혀졌다. 도망자들을 따라잡기까지 어느 정도의 시간이 걸릴까?
216|
217|길어야 반나절이다.
218|
219|‘있는 힘을 다해 도망쳤어야지. 뒤도 안 돌아보고. 거추장스러운 혹은 떼고 낙오자는 버리고 악착같이 뛰었어야지.’
220|
221|그랬다면 거리는 좁혀지지 않았을 것이다. 그러나 놈들은 방심했다. 폭설에 발이 묶였다고 생각했을 것이고, 그 차이가 지금의 상황을 만들었다.
222|
223|‘나는 좀 다르거든.’
224|
225|지난밤은 길었다. 추적에는 이골이 난 수하 중에서도 낙오자가 생길 정도였다. 폭설이 내리는 산중에서의 낙오란 죽음과 동의어다.
226|
227|전장에서의 죽음과 다른 점이 있다면 조금 천천히 죽는다는 것뿐이다. 그래서 조필은 지시했다.
228|
229|
230|
231|‘죽여.’
232|
233|
234|
235|호랑이는 죽어서 가죽을, 사람은 이름을 남긴다고 했다.
236|
237|하지만 조필의 생각은 달랐다. 일평생 뒷골목을 전전하던 삼류 인생에게 남길 이름이 있겠나. 가죽이라도 남겨야지.
238|
239|발가벗겨진 스무 구의 시신을 뒤로하고 그들은 계속 나아갔다. 그렇게 긴 밤이 끝나고 동틀 무렵, 놈들의 흔적을 발견할 수 있었다.
240|
241|‘곧 만날 수 있겠군, 친구.’
242|
243|조필의 입꼬리가 올라갔다. 오랜만에 그의 흥미를 끈 수수께끼의 고수다. 굳어 있던 심장이 펄떡거리며 뛰었다.
244|
245|
246|
247|* * *
248|
249|
250|

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
